newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Telebras hit by bribe scandal.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Telebras hit by bribe scandal.

text.p: Brazilian state telephone holding Telebras SA dropped Wednesday amid reports of a bribery scandal allegedly involving a leading Cabinet minister.
American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in the company fell 4-3/4 to 121-3/4. Telebras was among the most heavily traded shares on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning.

Traders cited a newspaper report that alleged Brazil Communications Minister Sergio Motta was involved in paying off lawmakers to secure votes for a bill letting reformist President Fernando Henrique Cardoso run for re-election.
Motta, a longtime Cardoso ally, is responsible for overseeing the privatization of the state-run telephone system.

Telebras "has had a pretty incredible run up and you don't know where ... (the corruption allegations) are going to go," a trader said. "It doesn't change anything fundamental for the stock medium- or long-term."
Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp rose 3-7/8 to 46-5/8 in very heavy trade after Merrill Lynch named it a focus one stock. Volume was 281,900 shares, more than 20 times normal daily trade.
Canada's Gandalf Technologies Inc was down 6/16 to 2-3/16 in heavy trade ahead of release of its first quarter earnings. Gandalf was among the most active shares on the Nasdaq exchange.
Canadian drilling equipment company Dreco Energy Services Ltd rose 7-5/8 to 46-1/8 after it agreed to merge with Houston's National-Oilwell Inc in a stock swap.
European oil ADRs largely strengthened. French companies Total SA rose two to 47-1/4 and Elf Aquitaine was up 7/8 to 52-1/4.
British Petroleum Co Plc rose 1-5/8 to 146-3/4, boosted by a stronger pound, traders said.
Dutch software company Baan fell four to 56-1/2 after the company announced it would buy Aurum Software Inc in a stock deal worth $250 million.
Advancers led decliners 279 to 195 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group rose 0.39 percent and volume in early afternoon was 43 million shares.
